markdown_report:
Select a **candidate-distribution stress audit** of the existing NextItNet before changing its architecture. At 0% progress, prioritize reproducible measurement; no supplied evidence establishes that audit improvements transfer to validation.

**Insights from the starting point.**

1. Recent deletion reduces margins more than older deletion across all categories. This measures sensitivity; it does not establish persistent older interests.
2. Negative-win rates of 2.60–6.38% describe training pairs. Plausible top-list competition and generalization remain unresolved.
3. Sampled causality and in-memory checks pass. Generated-predictor reload parity remains unverified and must precede ranking interpretation.

**Insights from related work.**

1. Sampled metrics can reverse comparisons [1]. Uniform sampling permits exact hypergeometric calibration; weighted and lexical sampling require empirical controls [4].
2. Difficult unobserved items can be positives [2]. Lexical similarity establishes neither irrelevance nor difficulty, and target-conditioned retrieval is an oracle diagnostic.
3. NextItNet supports unchanged causal scoring [3]. User-cluster intervals address repeated-prefix dependence, but omit checkpoint and item-population uncertainty [6].

These findings support candidate competition, temporal mechanism testing, and feedback grounding.

| Direction | Existing evidence | Next measurement | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Competition | Healthy sampled pairs | Count-matched candidate and catalog ranks | Generalization |
| Temporal mechanism | Recent-deletion sensitivity | Controlled residual interventions | Causal interpretation |
| Feedback grounding | Aggregate qualitative diagnosis | Evidence-linked rejection annotation | Unobserved intent and compatibility |

Three atomic ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty out of ten; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Critical assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Candidate stress audit [1,2] | 4/6/5 | Originality: useful integration, established components. Potential: exposes competition, transfer unproven. Difficulty: reusable scoring, substantial reproducibility controls. |
| Residual-branch fault calibration [3] | 5/6/6 | Originality: family-specific adaptation, established interventions. Potential: localizes defects, synthetic faults may mislead. Difficulty: accessible hooks, careful alignment required. |
| Feedback evidence ledger | 3/6/3 | Originality: task adaptation, standard annotation. Potential: distinguishes unknowns, twenty-user support is limited. Difficulty: simple schema, actual records and adjudication needed. |

**Selected algorithm.** Freeze at most 200 training users/category and five prefixes/user. Compare 99 unique uniform, training-frequency-weighted, prefix-conditioned lexical, and separately reported target-conditioned lexical competitors; retain full-catalog ranks on a fixed subset. Use identical eligible pools, deterministic ties, five frozen draws, explicit shortages, and logged lexical fallbacks. Exclude prefix-seen competitors while retaining repeated targets; annotate later-training positives without future-based filtering.

Fit category-local TF-IDF using only permitted titles/descriptions [5]. Lexical scores construct candidates exclusively. Report support, coverage, conflicts, rank quantiles, margins, and sampled/catalog hit disagreement by prefix length and training-frequency band. For uniform candidates, report expected sampled HR@10 as `hypergeom.cdf(9,N-1,r-1,99)` [4]; average users before categories. Bootstrap users within category, retaining their prefixes/draws [6].

These remain potentially memorized training diagnostics. Verify predictor parity, preserve all adapter interfaces and one checkpoint/category, and keep pinned macro validation HR@10 unchanged. Before further validation exposure, register at most one fixed negative-sampling intervention and one baseline comparison [7]. Metadata shortcuts, false negatives, and prior adaptive selection remain limitations.

idea.description: Extend the family-aware DiagnosisProbe with a frozen training-only candidate-distribution stress audit. Reuse one trained NextItNet per category to compare uniform, training-frequency-weighted, prefix-conditioned lexical, and separately labeled target-conditioned lexical competitors; calibrate uniform sampled ranks against exact catalog ranks on a bounded subset.
idea.motivation: Healthy sampled-pair separation and stronger recent-history sensitivity do not establish top-list specificity, deployment correctness, or benchmark HR@10. Controlled candidate construction can reveal competition concealed by easy sampled negatives without assuming current intent, satisfied needs, compatibility, or true negative labels. At the current early stage, this is a measurement proposal rather than an established accuracy intervention.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), existing supported metrics and definitions, and all host ModelView interfaces. view.model must remain the actual trained nn.Module. Retain view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence), and predict_score(features, items). Use permitted user_train histories and timestamps to identify users and construct diagnostic prefixes; loader rows alone do not identify users. Never consume unavailable ratings, reviews, item categories, prices, stores, hidden labels, other trials, or pretrained weights.

Freeze a manifest before examining audit outcomes. Within each category, sort stable user IDs and sample up to 200 eligible users without replacement using a diagnostic-local NumPy generator with seed 42. For each user, sample up to five distinct training target positions uniformly without replacement from positions having at least one preceding event, then sort positions. Every prefix contains only preceding training events and is truncated to the model's configured maximum length before left padding. Preserve repeated target events. Record user ID, target index, visible prefix IDs, target ID, category, item mapping, timestamps when available, and selection exclusions. These are fitted training targets, not a new holdout. Record checkpoint, metadata, manifest, and candidate-set hashes; record library versions and configuration.

For each example, define the eligible catalog as the category's mapped recommendable item IDs excluding padding, reserved tokens, and model-visible prefix items, then retain the target even when repeated in the prefix. Negative eligibility excludes the target. Do not filter using later events. Later occurrences within the available training history may be annotated afterward as known-positive conflicts, without changing primary pools, sample sizes, or ranks. Other unobserved candidates remain ambiguous. This resolves the earlier inconsistency between future-positive filtering and a prefix-conditioned diagnostic. Optional conflict-filtered summaries may report ranks after removal, with changed candidate counts and denominators; label them descriptive and do not compare their hit rates directly with the primary 100-candidate results. Never consult validation or test events for conflict annotation.

Require at least 99 eligible competitors for the primary comparison. Otherwise exclude that example from every primary condition and report the shortage and support loss; do not silently reduce candidate counts. Insert the target exactly once. Generate five frozen candidate draws using NumPy SeedSequence([42, category_index, sorted_user_index, target_position, condition_index, draw_index]); record category order, condition order, NumPy version, and actual candidate IDs. Uniform sampling is without replacement. Frequency sampling is sequential weighted sampling without replacement using weights equal to category training-interaction counts raised to 0.75; record counts, weights, algorithm, and draw order. These weights are not marginal inclusion probabilities. Fix manifests and candidate IDs across compared models.

Fit lexical representations independently per category on all permitted mapped catalog titles/descriptions from the supplied snapshot; this is unsupervised catalog metadata fitting, not additional interaction data. Normalize text using HTML entity decoding, tag removal, Unicode NFKC, lowercase, and collapsed whitespace; retain accents. Use separate title and description TfidfVectorizer instances with analyzer='word', ngram_range=(1,2), token_pattern='(?u)\\b\\w\\w+\\b', stop_words=None, min_df=1, max_df=1.0, max_features=100000 per field, binary=False, sublinear_tf=True, use_idf=True, smooth_idf=True, and norm='l2'. Record scikit-learn version, fitted vocabularies, IDFs, and cleaning implementation. Represent each item by L2-normalizing the concatenation of its title and description vectors, which gives equal field weight when both are nonzero. Use whichever field is available; handle an empty field vocabulary explicitly and report item zero-vector rates. No pretrained text encoder is needed.

The prefix lexical query is the L2-normalized arithmetic mean of visible-prefix item vectors, retaining repeated occurrences and using no recency weighting. The target query is the target item's vector and must be labeled oracle-conditioned: it measures separation from lexical lookalikes and is not a deployable retrieval method or evidence of history understanding. Prefix retrieval measures competition among established interests and may disadvantage genuine interest shifts. Rank eligible negatives by cosine dot product greater than zero, breaking ties by mapped item ID ascending. Take the first 99; for empty queries or insufficient positive-overlap candidates, fill remaining slots uniformly without replacement from remaining eligible IDs using the recorded local seed. Report query zero-vector rates, field coverage, positive-overlap counts, fallback fractions, and candidate similarity scores. Lexical top candidates are deterministic; repeated draws change only fallback slots and must not be presented as independent retrieval replicates. Keep every lexical score outside model prediction and the pinned evaluator.

Use no_grad and evaluation mode; preserve and restore all module training flags and any altered RNG states or hooks in finally. Diagnostic RNGs must not alter the training stream. Extract features at the largest index whose sequence ID is nonzero, never count-1; exclude all-padding rows explicitly. Compute original target and candidate scores with the same compatibility scoring path. Check score finiteness and record exclusions consistently across paired conditions. Report sampled target rank, HR@10, reciprocal rank, positive-minus-maximum-competitor margin, and paired differences. Raw margins remain score-scale dependent and are not benchmark metrics.

Prespecify a catalog subset: uniformly choose at most 40 of the selected users/category with a separate local seed 4242, and use each selected user's earliest manifest prefix. Score all eligible catalog items in chunks of 4096, retaining the target and using the identical universe for sampled and exact comparisons. Use the host's total tie ordering when exposed. Otherwise define diagnostic ordering as score descending then mapped item ID ascending, document that it is not necessarily benchmark-equivalent, and use it everywhere in the audit. For target score s_y, exact rank is 1 plus the count of items with score greater than s_y or equal score and smaller mapped ID. Do not use tolerance-based equality for ranking.

Let N be eligible catalog size including the target and r its exact rank. For m=99 uniformly sampled distinct competitors, X follows Hypergeom(N-1,r-1,m), and expected diagnostic sampled HR@10 equals scipy.stats.hypergeom.cdf(9,N-1,r-1,m). This assumes the fixed total ordering above. If randomized ties are required, integrate over their outcomes instead of substituting strict-score rank. Compute calibration only on catalog-subset examples. Compare the analytic probability with mean empirical uniform hits over frozen draws; report residuals without treating five draws as precise individual calibration. Do not apply the ordinary hypergeometric formula to weighted or lexical candidates. Full-catalog ranks and 100-candidate hit rates are distinct estimands, so their disagreement is expected and is not itself a model defect.

Prespecify prefix-length strata 1-4, 5-9, 10-19, and at least 20. Form item-frequency bands from category training counts: sort items by ascending (count, mapped ID), then split the ordered catalog into three approximately equal item-count bands. Record boundaries and label them tail, middle, and head. Report example/user counts, exclusions, conflict rates, metadata coverage, fallback rates, rank quantiles, paired margins, and sampled/full-catalog hit disagreement by these strata. Empty measurements return null and zero support. Aggregate draws within prefix and prefixes within user, then users within category, then equally across all four categories; do not silently omit a category with no support. State this diagnostic user-weighted estimand explicitly.

Use 1,000 paired user-cluster bootstrap replicates with a separate local seed 42: resample users within category and retain all their selected prefixes and frozen draws. Report percentile 95% intervals for prespecified aggregate differences. These intervals condition on fitted checkpoints, selected users/prefixes, fixed candidates, metadata, and catalog; they omit training-seed and item-population uncertainty and do not fully address shared-item dependence. Do not infer user-level intervals from unidentified loader rows.

Before interpreting audit rankings, perform a separate host-authorized generated-predictor reload check on identical category routes, mappings, truncation, left padding, histories, and candidate lists. Cover every category, short and maximum-length prefixes, repeated histories, and the final-position readout. For float32 scores, prespecify rtol=1e-4 and atol=1e-5; record maximum error, finiteness, score agreement, and exact ordered top-10 agreement under the diagnostic tie policy. Score tolerance does not guarantee rank agreement. Investigate any failure before interpretation; report near-tie instability separately rather than hiding it. The adapter must return deployment parity as unavailable when no reload interface exists, distinguishing it from in-memory parity.

The interpreter must embed measured metrics, definitions, support, selection configuration, and missingness; separate training memorization, candidate sensitivity, qualitative feedback, and independent validation. Optional feedback-ledger work needs actual recommendation and feedback records, exact evidence snippets, two independent annotators, agreement, and adjudication. Aggregate diagnosis alone cannot establish user-level intent or compatibility. Keep the twenty training simulator users and their full-catalog unseen-item recommendations separate from validation evidence.

If pursuing a training intervention, register its code/configuration and expected effect before further validation exposure: replace only training-negative selection with a fixed 50% uniform and 50% count^0.75 mixture, sampling from baseline-authorized negative pools without replacement where multiple negatives are used. Reuse the baseline's negative count, loss, optimizer, architecture, epochs, and batches; do not add a separately fitted scoring component. The hypothesis is improved rank discrimination against frequency-weighted diagnostic competitors; uniform and lexical performance may worsen, and false-negative risk remains. Train one replacement NextItNet checkpoint/category and perform one aggregate comparison against the supplied corrected baseline with unchanged pinned validation candidates. Compare fixed final checkpoints unless the supplied baseline requires a specific existing checkpoint-selection rule; retain that rule and log its validation exposure. Report per-category and macro HR@10. Compute paired validation-user bootstrap differences only if the host legitimately supplies per-user outcomes; otherwise report uncertainty as unavailable. Log earlier validation exposure and stop after the registered comparison; this limits additional adaptation without undoing prior selection bias. Do not reuse another trial's checkpoint or select a model using training audit scores alone.

Preserve Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl and dataset routing. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; artifacts stay trial-local. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, and 200 batches per epoch; use single-GPU execution and bound all audit inference within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Load exactly one independently trained NextItNet checkpoint per category, without ensembles, checkpoint averaging, or independent score fusion. This audit changes no architecture; any later architecture or inference change must update the embedded predictor writer and family-specific probes consistently.
idea.pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        saved_modes = capture_all_module_training_flags(self.view.model)
        self.view.model.eval()
        try:
            with torch.no_grad():
                metrics, definitions = existing_family_specific_probes(train_loader)
                manifest = load_or_freeze_training_manifest(
                    self.view.user_train, seed=42,
                    max_users_per_category=200, max_prefixes_per_user=5)
                text_index = fit_or_load_category_local_tfidf(
                    permitted_titles_and_descriptions, recorded_configuration)
                candidate_manifest = freeze_candidate_sets(
                    manifest, conditions=['uniform', 'frequency_075',
                                          'prefix_lexical', 'target_lexical_oracle'],
                    negatives=99, draws=5, seed_scheme=recorded_seed_scheme,
                    exclude_visible_prefix=True, filter_future_events=False)
                catalog_subset = freeze_user_subset(
                    manifest, max_users=40, one_earliest_manifest_prefix=True,
                    seed=4242)

                for example in manifest:
                    sequence = truncate_then_left_pad(example.prefix)
                    t = largest_nonzero_index(sequence)
                    if t is None or example.eligible_competitor_count < 99:
                        record_common_exclusion(example)
                        continue
                    features = self.view.log2feats(sequence[None, :])[0, t]
                    for condition, draws in candidate_manifest[example.id].items():
                        for draw in draws:
                            ids = [example.target] + draw.unique_negative_ids
                            scores = self.view.predict_score(features, tensor(ids))
                            record_rank_hit_rr_and_max_competitor_margin(
                                scores, ids, tie_policy=recorded_total_order)
                            annotate_later_training_positive_conflicts(
                                draw, example, modify_primary_candidates=False)

                    if example.id in catalog_subset:
                        N, r = exact_target_rank_by_chunked_scoring(
                            self.view, features, example.eligible_catalog,
                            target=example.target, chunk_size=4096,
                            tie_policy=recorded_total_order)
                        expected_uniform_hit = scipy.stats.hypergeom.cdf(
                            9, N - 1, r - 1, 99)
                        record_catalog_and_uniform_calibration(
                            example, N, r, expected_uniform_hit)

                summaries = aggregate_draws_then_prefixes_then_users_then_categories()
                intervals = paired_user_cluster_bootstrap(
                    summaries.source_records, replicates=1000, seed=42)
                return {
                    'metrics': merge(metrics, summaries, intervals,
                                     support_missingness_and_configuration()),
                    'metric_definitions': merge(
                        definitions, explicit_training_diagnostic_definitions())
                }
        finally:
            remove_temporary_diagnostic_hooks()
            restore_all_module_training_flags(saved_modes)


def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return build_prompt_with_measured_metrics_and_definitions(
        raw_diagnosis,
        require_support_configuration_and_missingness=True,
        distinguish_oracle_from_prefix_conditioning=True,
        state_training_memorization_and_false_negative_ambiguity=True,
        forbid_inferring_benchmark_HR_or_unobserved_user_needs=True)

# Separate host-authorized prerequisite:
# Reload generated working/predict.py; compare scores and ordered top-10
# against the actual trained category model on identical mapped inputs.
# Record unavailable status if the host provides no reload interface.

# Optional next experiment, registered before further validation exposure:
# Change only negative sampling to fixed 50% uniform / 50% count^0.75.
# Train one replacement NextItNet checkpoint/category with fixed seeds/budgets.
# Compare once with the supplied baseline using pinned macro validation HR@10.
# Deploy exactly one checkpoint/category; never fuse model scores.

originality.positive: Integrates family-specific predictor verification, candidate controls, oracle-versus-prefix lexical queries, and analytic uniform-sampling calibration in one reproducible diagnostic protocol.
originality.negative: The statistical identities, retrieval methods, ranking audits, and intervention controls are established; integration is the principal contribution.

future_potential.positive: Can identify misleading sampled-pair conclusions and support a narrowly registered single-model training intervention while preserving the benchmark.
future_potential.negative: No evidence establishes that training-audit improvements predict validation gains; memorization, false negatives, metadata shortcuts, and shared-item dependence limit interpretation.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses frozen NextItNet scoring, standard sparse TF-IDF, SciPy distributions, and bounded catalog inference without another fitted recommendation model.
code_difficulty.negative: Stable manifests, exact candidate counts, deterministic ties, user-cluster aggregation, metadata fallbacks, and generated-predictor verification require substantial careful integration.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: [1] Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can produce comparisons inconsistent with full-catalog evaluation.
Motivates explicit candidate-count controls and sampled-versus-catalog diagnostic comparisons.
limitations: Does not establish a defect in the supplied NextItNet or predict which intervention will improve its validation score.
Does not justify altering the pinned RecHarness evaluator.

related_work.title: Hard-BPR
contributions: [2] Examines false-negative risks associated with difficult unobserved recommendation items.
Motivates treating lexical and frequency-weighted competitors as ambiguous rather than confirmed preference errors.
limitations: Does not supply true negative labels or compatibility judgments for this task.
Its training method is not implemented by the proposed diagnostic and would require a separate registered comparison.

related_work.title: NextItNet: A Simple Convolutional Generative Network for Next Item Recommendation
contributions: [3] Introduces causal dilated convolutional modeling for next-item recommendation.
Provides the retained backbone and residual intervention sites for family-specific diagnostics.
limitations: Architecture alone does not establish immediate intent, satisfied needs, or practical item compatibility.
Published performance does not establish results under the supplied RecHarness splits and candidate protocol.

related_work.title: SciPy hypergeom distribution documentation
contributions: [4] Defines the hypergeometric distribution and its cumulative distribution function.
Supports exact expected sampled HR@10 calculation for uniform sampling of 99 distinct competitors under a fixed total ranking.
limitations: The ordinary hypergeometric formula does not describe frequency-weighted or lexical candidate construction.
Calibration requires the same filtered catalog, candidate count, target, and tie ordering for exact and sampled ranks.

related_work.title: scikit-learn TfidfVectorizer documentation
contributions: [5] Documents tokenization, n-gram, TF scaling, IDF smoothing, vocabulary, and normalization options.
Provides a reproducible local lexical representation without pretrained weights.
limitations: Lexical overlap does not establish user preference, incompatibility, or difficulty for NextItNet.
Missing descriptions, repeated titles, and franchise vocabulary can produce coverage bias and shortcuts.

related_work.title: The Pigeonhole Bootstrap
contributions: [6] Examines uncertainty estimation for dependent observations with crossed structure, relevant to recommender data.
Motivates retaining repeated observations within users and explicitly stating remaining dependence assumptions.
limitations: A user-cluster bootstrap is a restricted practical choice and does not implement the paper's complete crossed-dependence treatment.
The proposed intervals omit training-seed variation, item-population uncertainty, and some dependence induced by shared items.

related_work.title: The Reusable Holdout: Preserving Validity in Adaptive Data Analysis
contributions: [7] Explains how adaptive reuse of holdout information can undermine generalization claims.
Motivates preregistering one intervention, logging validation exposure, and limiting additional comparisons.
limitations: A one-comparison cap does not implement a reusable-holdout mechanism or erase earlier adaptive selection bias.
Registration alone does not guarantee statistical validity or validation improvement.
